newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end mostly down on stronger yen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end mostly down on stronger yen.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures closed mostly lower on Friday, as the yen's gains against the dollar offset the stronger Chicago market overnight, traders said.

The most active March 1998 contract was down 130 yen at 15,870 yen per tonne. The spot May 1997 contract fell by its daily 500 yen limit to 17,320 yen in early afternoon, but recovered later to close at 17,590.

Active selling from individual investors depressed most months from the opening, traders said. "Light technical buying supported some contracts later. But we expect further losses if the yen remains stronger next week," a brokerage trader said.
On the CBOT Project A overnight trading system, most-active March corn futures traded at $2.94-3/4 per bushel as of 0725 GMT, down from $2.96 at Thursday's close.
CBOT Project A March soybeans stood at $7.79-1/4 per bushel, down from $7.83-1/4 on Thursday.
